lessons.fullText:
Lesson 41: Dealing with Teenagers 
 
Helen is angry at her teenage son, Thomas, for coming home late. Listen to their 
conversation and mark the statements below “True” or “False.” 
 
Listening Comprehension 
True or false according to the conversation? 
1. Helen forgot to remind Thomas what time he was supposed to be home 
2. Thomas is over an hour late 
3. Thomas' punishment is that he can’t use the car for the rest of the 
month 
4. Thomas got into an accident and broke his leg 
5. It was Thomas' stepfather who suggested the eleven o'clock curfew 
6. Thomas got his car from his stepfather 
7. The car is still on the side of the road 
8. Thomas didn't have his phone with him 
9. He hitchhiked to get home 
10. Thomas had been texting his girlfriend at 2 AM 
 
 


 
 
Conversation Text 
 
Helen: Was there some part about ‘Be home 
before eleven’ that you didn’t understand? I 
thought I was crystal clear. In fact, I distinctly 
remember double-checking with you right 
before you left to be sure that you heard me.  
 
Thomas: Aw, gimme a break, mom – it’s only 
11:20! 
 
Helen: Wrong answer, young man. Now go to 
your room. You’ve lost your driving privileges 
for the rest of the month.  
 
Thomas: Really? You’re not even going to give 
me the chance to explain? I might have driven 
the car into a ditch, broken my leg, and had to 
crawl all the way back home – but because I 
got in after eleven, you’d still chew me out.  
 
Helen: Nice try. But your leg’s not broken and 
you weren’t crawling.  
 
crystal clear = very 
clear 
 
double-checking = 
checking a second 
time, to make sure of 
something 
 
gimme a break = 
don’t be so harsh on 
me (or: that’s 
ridiculous) 
 
privileges = special 
advantages or 
benefits 
 
ditch = a long, narrow 
hole in the ground 
(such as one 
alongside a road) 
 
crawl = move on your 
hands and knees 
instead of walking 
upright 
 
chew me out = 
reprimand, scold 
 
Vocabulary 


 
 
Thomas: There’s, like, no other seventeen-
year-old on the face of the planet who has an 
eleven-o-clock curfew. Honestly, do I look like 
I’m ten years old?  
 
Helen: You certainly act like it sometimes. And 
why on earth would I allow a later curfew when 
you can’t even keep the one we agreed on?  
 
Thomas: I never agreed to it. You had that 
conversation with Hank – it was his brilliant 
idea. I didn’t even get a say in the matter. 
 
Helen: You know, it wouldn’t kill you to talk 
about your stepfather a little nicer from time to 
time. Does it ever cross your mind how much 
he sacrifices for you? He’s the reason you got a 
car in the first place. 
 
Thomas: Yeah, but the only reason he gave it to 
me was because no used car salesman with half 
a brain would take it off his hands. He’s had 
that piece of crap since he was my age. 
 
Helen: Just keep talking the way you are and 
your ‘crappy’ car will turn into ‘no’ car.  
 
curfew = a time 
before which you 
must be at home 
 
I didn’t even get a 
say in the matter = I 
didn’t get to express 
my opinion or 
contribute to the 
decision-making 
 
it wouldn’t kill you to 
= a sarcastic way to 
say “it would be good 
if you behaved 
differently” 
 
cross your mind = 
when a thought 
comes into your head 
 
take it off his hands = 
buy or receive it from 
him 
 
piece of crap = 
something terrible or 
in bad condition 
(slightly offensive) 
 
Vocabulary 


 
 
Thomas: Threats and punishments. That’s 
real mature, mom.  
 
Helen: You know what, wise guy? Hand 
over the keys. Right now. Let’s make that 
two months without going out.  
 
Thomas: Fine. You want ‘em? Take ‘em. The 
car’s not even in the garage, anyway. 
 
Helen: What do you mean? 
 
Thomas: I mean that my tire blew out and 
that heap of junk is sitting on the roadside, 
waiting for the tow truck. 
 
Helen: Oh for God’s sake, son! Why didn’t 
you call me? 
 
Thomas: Remember last Thursday when 
you took away my phone?  
 
Helen: But why didn’t you borrow one from 
your friends? And how did you even get 
home? If you tell me you hitchhiked I swear 
I’m going to have a heart attack.  
 
wise guy = a person who 
is acting arrogant and 
sarcastic, like he knows 
everything 
 
hand over = give 
 
my tire blew out = the 
tire (wheel of the car) 
exploded 
 
heap of junk = a sarcastic 
way to refer to a car or 
piece of machinery that 
isn’t functioning well, 
implying it is a pile of 
garbage 
 
tow truck = the truck 
that can take a disabled 
car to the mechanic 
 
hitchhiked = got a ride 
from a stranger by 
standing by the side of 
the road and signaling to 
passing cars 
 
Vocabulary 


 
 
Thomas: Okay, okay. I hailed a cab. Relax. 
 
Helen: Well, that’s a relief. But why didn’t 
you tell me that in the first place? Of course 
I’m not going to ground you for getting a 
flat tire! 
 
Thomas: But you’re always trying to punish 
me before you even know all the details! 
Like when you took my phone away. Do you 
know why I was texting at two in the 
morning? I was helping Bethany with her 
organic chemistry homework because she’s 
almost failing the class. 
 
Helen: I’m sorry. But how am I supposed to 
know if you don’t tell me these things?  
 
Thomas: If you’ll actually listen, then I’ll start talking.  
 
Helen: All right. Now go get some sleep – we’ll deal with the car in the 
morning.  
 
 
 
 
 
hailed a cab = signaled to 
a passing taxi to stop and 
pick me up 
 
ground you = give a 
punishment where you 
are forbidden from going 
out 
 
flat tire = when the car’s 
tire loses its air 
 
texting = sending text 
messages on a cell phone 
Vocabulary 


 
 
Vocabulary Quiz 
Complete each sentence with a word from the box. Two words are not used. 
chewed me out 
crystal clear 
gimme a break 
have a say 
crawled 
double-check 
grounded 
piece of crap 
crossed my mind 
flat tire 
hand over 
texting 
 
1. _______________________ the money, and I'll give you the information you're 
looking for. 
2. The baby _______________________ towards the teddy bear on the other side 
of the room. 
3. I bought this blender three days ago and it's already broken. What a 
_______________________! 
4. How can they give me a huge project today and insist that it needs to be 
done by tomorrow? _______________________! 
5. If something doesn't add up on the financial spreadsheet, I can have my 
accountant _______________________  the numbers. 
6. _______________________ while driving is very dangerous because it 
distracts you from the road. 
7. I accidentally sent a confidential e-mail to the wrong person. My boss 
_______________________ for that one! 
8. The instructions in the training manual need to be _______________________ 
in order to avoid mistakes and misunderstandings. 
9. We got a _______________________ after running over some broken glass in 
the road. 
10. I think university students should _______________________ in matters of 
school policy. 
 


 
 
Speaking Task 
There is a big debate about whether spanking young children (hitting them 
on their butt as punishment) is appropriate, or unnecessarily violent. What is 
your opinion? Also talk about what kind of punishments your parents used 
when you were a child/teenager.  
 
Record your answer at www.speakpipe.com/espressoenglish or send the 
MP3 to homework@espressoenglish.net for feedback. 
 
Answers 
Comprehension Questions 
1. False

3. True 
4. False 
5. True 
6. True 
7. True 
8. True 
9. False 
10. False 
Vocabulary Quiz

3. piece of crap

Lesson 42: Discussing the News 
 
Two roommates, Patrick and Winston, discuss their newspaper subscription and news 
in general. Listen to their conversation and mark the statements below “True” or 
“False.” 
 
Listening Comprehension 
True or false according to the dialogue? 
1. Patrick doesn't remember the e-mail Winston sent 
2. The Springtime Examiner subscription has already expired 
3. Winston is not sure whether or not he will renew it 
4. Patrick is distracted by a text from a friend 
5. Patrick likes getting news instantly 
6. Winston dislikes online news because staring at a screen is bad for your eyes 
7. Winston admits that instant notifications are good in emergencies 
8. Winston is concerned that people are losing the ability to think critically 
9. Patrick believes that change is inevitable 
10. Patrick and Winston will split the cost of the newspaper subscription 
 
 


 
 
Conversation Text 
 
Winston: Hey Patrick, did you get the email I 
forwarded you last week?  
 
Patrick: Umm, I’m not sure… what was it 
about? Could you refresh my memory? 
 
Winston: The message saying that our 
Springtime Examiner subscription expires at 
the end of the month. 
 
Patrick: You’re not seriously considering 
renewing it, are you? 
 
Winston: I’m definitely renewing it. What I 
want to know is if you’re gonna chip in. 
 
Patrick: Oh, come on, Winston, get with the 
times! Pretty much everyone in our 
generation gets their news online.  
 
Winston: You can’t call that news. What 
people read online is fluff. It’s like pure sugar 
that rots your brain, with a few facts thrown 
forwarded = received an e-
mail from someone else and 
re-sent it to a new person 
 
refresh my memory = remind 
me 
 
expires = comes to an end, 
isn’t valid anymore 
 
renewing = to renew a 
subscription means to pay for 
it and keep it active for 
another period of time in the 
future 
 
chip in = contribute money to 
a shared expense 
 
get with the times! = 
update/modernize yourself 
 
fluff = (slang) content that 
isn’t meaningful, it just exists 
to fill up space 
 
rots = makes something 
decay, decompose 
 
 
Vocabulary 


 
 
in to make you think you’re staying abreast 
of the news. Plus, the internet plays fast and 
loose with the facts. 
 
Patrick: (distracted) Ah!  
 
Winston: What? 
 
Patrick: The little software company I 
invested in last week – it’s on the upswing. I 
get notifications about stocks on my phone. 
 
Winston: See? Case in point! You can’t even 
follow our conversation because you’re 
distracted by your notifications. It’s another 
thing that bugs me. Everything is so 
instantaneous. Do you have to know what’s 
happening with your stocks at this very 
moment? Why can’t it wait until tomorrow?  
 
Patrick: Because I don’t want to wait until 
tomorrow. Why should I? That’s one of the 
perks of living in the twenty-first century. 
Something can happen on the other side of the 
world, and the news reaches me in a flash.  
 
staying abreast of = staying 
updated, accompanying the 
latest information 
 
plays fast and loose with the 
facts = does not carefully 
check or prove 
 
on the upswing = on a trend 
of increase or improvement 
 
stocks = elements of the stock 
market, the state of the 
economy 
 
Case in point! = this is a good 
example of what I was just 
talking about 
 
bugs me = annoys, bothers 
me 
 
perks = benefits 
 
in a flash = very quickly, 
instantly 
Vocabulary 


 
 
Winston: Yeah, you learn the bare 
essentials, but the coverage leaves a lot to 
be desired. They take one or two points and 
talk about them to death. So you might find 
out that there was an earthquake in California, 
or a volatile situation in the Middle East, but – 
 
Patrick: You’re saying that’s not important? 
What if your brother was in California when 
the earthquake hit? You’d want to know he 
was safe as soon as you could! 
 
Winston: Well, sure. That’s what technology 
should be used for: spreading the word in 
emergencies. But when it comes to a 
complex, serious issue, a few soundbites or a 
simple notification just won’t cut it. Not 
everything can be boiled down to a few bullet 
points to browse on your phone. 
 
Patrick: But it doesn’t hurt to have the bullet 
points.  
 
Winston: Yes! Yes! It absolutely does hurt! If 
you dumb things down for quick 
consumption, people are going to get used to 
it. They’re going to start thinking a political 
bare essentials = basic 
facts/fundamentals 
 
leaves a lot to be desired = is 
not as good as it should be 
 
talk about them to death = 
talk about them excessively 
 
volatile = unstable and may 
“explode” 
 
spreading the word = sharing 
information with many 
people 
 
when it comes to = an 
informal way to say 
“regarding” 
 
soundbite = a very short 
audio or video clip 
 
won’t cut it = won’t be 
sufficient 
 
boiled down = summarized, 
reduced to the essentials 
 
browse = look at casually 
 
dumb things down = make 
things overly simple 
Vocabulary 


 
 
campaign or a pressing social issue can be 
squeezed into the amount of space it takes to 
read the weather forecast. People already 
have a much shorter attention span, and our 
critical thinking skills are going downhill, 
too.  
 
Patrick: You may have a point, but you’re 
swimming against the current. People aren’t 
going to go back to reading dense papers if 
they can stay informed with less effort. Things 
change. Newspapers were once the height of 
progress, and now they’re becoming 
antiquated.  
 
Winston: Well, I’m still going to renew my 
Springtime Examiner. 
 
Patrick: I figured you would. But you’re on 
your own for the subscription fee.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
pressing = urgent, needing 
immediate attention 
 
squeezed = compressed into 
a small space 
 
attention span = the amount 
of time someone is able to 
focus on something 
 
going downhill = becoming 
worse 
 
swimming against the 
current = going against the 
trend or the majority of 
people (also: swimming 
against the tide) 
 
antiquated = old-fashioned, 
no longer relevant 
 
you’re on your own = you’re 
responsible; you won’t have 
help 
Vocabulary 


 
 
Vocabulary Quiz 
Complete each sentence with a word from the box. Three words are not used. 
browsing 
leave a lot to be desired 
squeezed 
bugging 
on the upswing 
staying abreast of 
chipping in 
on your own 
stocks 
expired 
perks 
to death 
in a flash 
pressing 
won't cut it 
 
1. All our relatives are _________________________ to buy a new TV for grandma. 
2. I won't have time to cook today, so you're _________________________ for dinner. 
3. His table manners _________________________. He was chewing with his mouth 
open, for goodness' sake! 
4. I enjoy _________________________ at the bookstore, even though I never buy 
anything. 
5. The number of people buying homes is _________________________, so construction 
companies are building more housing. 
6. If someone breaks into your house, this security system will alert the police 
_________________________. 
7. Getting to visit new places is one of the _________________________ of being a flight 
attendant. 
8. I've got a song stuck in my head and it's been _________________________ me all 
day! 
9. Sorry, you can't use this coupon. It _________________________ yesterday. 
10. The ride wasn't very comfortable because there were nearly a hundred 
people _________________________ into the bus. 
11. We don't have much time for this meeting, so let's talk about the most 
_________________________ concerns first. 
12. If the company wants to hire someone with a doctorate, then my master's 
degree _________________________. 


 
 
Speaking Task 
Do you identify more with Patrick or with Winston? Explain your beliefs on “instant 
notifications” and our relationship with technology. Do you tend to be an early 
adopter (use new technology as soon as it comes out) or do you prefer the old-
fashioned ways of doing things?  
 
Record your answer at www.speakpipe.com/espressoenglish or send the MP3 to 
homework@espressoenglish.net

1. True

9. True 
10. False

2. on your own 
3. leave a lot to be desired 
4. browsing

Lesson 43: Surprise! 
 
Sarah is planning a surprise birthday party for her sister, Amy. She gets Amy’s 
boyfriend Jake to help. Listen to their conversation and answer these questions: 
 
Comprehension Questions 
1. Sarah told everyone to arrive at... 
a. 5:30 
b. 6:00 
c. 7:00 
2. Jake says that the guests... 
a. might ruin the surprise 
b. will probably be late 
c. won't remember to bring food 
3. Jake's job is to... 
a. cook dinner 
b. get Amy out of the house 
c. make the party decorations 
4. Jake describes Amy as... 
a. romantic 
b. shy 
c. stubborn 
5. Sarah is not sure that... 
a. Jake and Amy can afford the expense of a puppy 
b. Amy will be happy to get the puppy 
c. the puppy will behave itself during the party 
6. Sarah says the puppy has... 
a. been aggressive 
b. destroyed some of her stuff 
c. tried to run away 
7. Jake doesn't want to kidnap Amy or fake a medical emergency 
because... 
a. It would be too complicated to organize 
b. she might come back to the house too early 
c. she would be angry about the deception 
 


 
 
Conversation Text 
 
Jake: Okay, fill me in on the plan. 
 
Sarah: I told everyone to be here at 6 
o’clock sharp. 
 
Jake: Yeah… that’s wishful thinking. 
Nobody’s going to show up that soon 
after work. Especially with the traffic 
jams during rush hour. 
 
Sarah: Oh, I know. I said six because 
we’re really shooting for seven. I just 
need you to make sure Amy’s outta here 
by 5:30 so that I can get everything set 
up. 
 
Jake: And what if she doesn’t want to go 
anywhere? 
 
Sarah: Then don’t ask her to go, just 
whisk her away to a romantic birthday 
dinner with you. 
 
Jake: Come on, you know Amy. If I try to 
force her, she’ll dig her heels in. 
 
Sarah: Okay, then guilt her into it 
somehow. 
 
Jake: Guilt her? How am I supposed to 
do that?

about the details I am 
missing

wishful thinking =

probably not going to 
happen

Getting her out of the house is your job. I’ve 
done everything else. All the invitations, the 
catering, watching the puppy . . . 
 
Jake: Thanks for that, by the way. I owe you 
one. 
 
Sarah: I still have my doubts about this puppy 
thing. Are you absolutely sure she wants a 
puppy?  
 
Jake: Trust me. She wants the puppy. Who 
doesn’t love a surprise puppy? 
 
Sarah: I mean, that’s a lot of responsibility to 
just spring on a person. 
 
Jake: She’s dying to get a dog. She’s been 
nagging me about it for months, and I’ve been 
giving her the runaround.  
 
Sarah: What if it’s not the kind of dog she 
wants? 
 
Jake: She doesn’t care what kind of dog it is, she 
just wants something cute and furry. And this 
puppy is adorable. 
 
Sarah: Well, your adorable puppy chewed on 
my shoes and peed on my rug. 
 
Jake: Yeah, sorry about that. I’ll make it up to 
you, I promise.

professional food 
preparation/serving 
at a party or event 
 
I owe you one = I will 
do a favor for you in 
return for the favor 
you did for me 
 
spring on = surprise 
someone with 
 
nagging me = 
reminding me in a 
persistent, annoying 
way 
 
giving her the 
runaround = giving 
her excuses and 
answers that avoid 
the main issue or 
avoid making a 
commitment 
 
furry = full of fur 
(animal body hair) 
 
peed = urinated 
 
I’ll make it up to you 
= I’ll compensate for 
the problem/damage 
Vocabulary 


 
 
Sarah: Just… make sure she’s not here from 
five-thirty to seven. Whatever you have to do. 
Kidnap her. Fake a medical emergency. Get 
yourself arrested and call her to bail you out. 
Whatever. 
 
Jake: Hmm, those ideas would probably 
backfire. She’d be mad if she found out I lied to 
her. How about I just take her to dinner? 
 
Sarah: Yes! Exactly. Stop overthinking it; she’ll 
be thrilled if you wine and dine her.  
 
Jake: Okay. I’ll text you when we’re on our way 
home from dinner. Anything else? 
 
Sarah: That’s it. You distract Amy for a couple of 
hours, and I’ll take care of the rest. 
 
Jake: All right. She’s going to be blown away by 
this surprise party – I can’t wait! 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
kidnap = forcefully 
take someone and 
hold them prisoner 
against their will 
 
bail you out = pay a 
sum of money to get 
someone out of jail 
 
backfire = fail with 
an unintended bad 
result 
 
wine and dine her = 
take her to a very 
fancy restaurant and 
treat her very nicely 
 
be blown away = 
very surprised and 
impressed

Lesson 44: An Argument 
 
Listen to this argument between two roommates, Nadia and Elizabeth, and choose the 
best answer to each comprehension question: 
 
Listening Comprehension 
1. Nadia isn't feeling well because she has... 
a. a hangover 
b. a headache 
c. the flu 
2. Elizabeth was woken up by... 
a. loud music from the living room 
b. Nadia making too much noise 
c. the strange girl on the couch 
3. In the future, Elizabeth wants Nadia... 
a. to clean up the mess she makes 
b. not to stay out so late 
c. to pay more for the extra food she eats 
4. Elizabeth is anxious because... 
a. Nadia appears to be very sick 
b. her boyfriend is coming for lunch 
c. the kitchen is dangerous 
5. Nadia's friend Alice also... 
a. lost Elizabeth's book 
b. ruined Elizabeth's book 
c. stole Elizabeth's book 
6. Nadia promises to... 
a. ask her friends to behave better 
b. get the bookshelf fixed 
c. replace Elizabeth's book 
7. Elizabeth and Nadia agree that... 
a. their friends don't get along with each other 
b. they can't stand living together 
c. they need to take better care of the apartment 


 
 
Conversation Text 
 
Elizabeth: Hey Nadia, are you awake? I need 
to ask you something. 
 
Nadia: Ugh, can’t it wait? I’ve got a 
pounding headache. 
 
Elizabeth: Are you hung over again? 
 
Nadia: No, it’s just a migraine. And you 
barging into my room isn’t helping. 
 
Elizabeth: I’d just like to know why there’s a 
complete stranger sleeping on the couch in 
the living room, with my blanket. She was 
snoring so loud that she woke me up. 
 
Nadia: Oh. That’s Alice. We got home really 
late last night and I told her she could crash 
here.  
 
Elizabeth: Well, that’s very generous of you. 
But the next time you volunteer our 
apartment as a bed and breakfast, could you 
at least clean up the kitchen afterwards?  
 
Nadia: Yeah… we were starving when we got 
back from the club, and by the time we 
finished making the food, we were just too 
pooped to put everything away. 
 
Elizabeth: Honestly Nadia, I don’t need to 
hear the whole backstory. All I care about is 
can't it wait? = a slightly rude 
way to say you don’t think 
something is urgent 
 
a pounding headache = a 
headache in which you 
experience pulses or waves of 
pain 
 
hung over = feeling sick and 
tired due to drinking too much 
alcohol the night before 
 
a migraine = a very strong 
type of headache 
 
barging into = entering rudely 
without asking permission 
 
snoring = making loud 
breathing sounds while 
sleeping 
 
crash = (informal) sleep, stay 
over at someone’s house 
 
starving = very hungry 
 
pooped = very tired 
 
backstory = the events that 
happened before 
Vocabulary 


 
 
that right now the stove is encrusted with dried 
pancake batter, and all the coffee cups reek of 
whiskey.   
 
Nadia: Uh, sorry about that. We’ll clean it up later, just 
gimme a few more minutes to sleep in. 
 
Elizabeth: No, I need you to clean it up now! My 
boyfriend’s coming over for lunch, and the kitchen 
looks like a bomb went off in there! 
 
Nadia: We’ll get to it, all right? But it’s seven in the 
morning, there’s still plenty of time. 
 
Elizabeth: It’s a quarter to eleven!  
 
Nadia: Okay, okay! Geez, you always blow a fuse 
whenever I do the slightest little thing to annoy you. 
 
Elizabeth: The slightest little thing?! You invited a 
random girl over, trashed the apartment, and by the 
way Alice also spilled water all over my Victorian 
poetry book. The pages are sopping wet. 
 
Nadia: Well, it serves you right for leaving your stuff 
lying all over the floor. We’ve got shelves for all your 
junk.  
 
Elizabeth: Not anymore. The bookshelf broke when 
that fat friend of yours tried climbing up it to get the 
cat down from the top! 
 
Nadia: Oh, right. Um… I’ll call the guy tomorrow to get 
it fixed. 
 
encrusted = when a 
sticky substance 
dries and forms a 
crust on a surface 
 
batter = the thick 
liquid used to make 
pancakes and cakes 
 
reek of = smell very 
badly of 
 
sleep in = sleep until 
a later time than 
usual 
 
blow a fuse = get 
angry; explode with 
anger 
 
trashed = (slang) 
damage or destroy 
 
sopping wet = 
completely wet; full 
of water 
 
it serves you right = 
you deserve the bad 
thing that happened 
to you 
Vocabulary 


 
 
Elizabeth: You said you’d do that last week, but you 
never did!  
 
Nadia: It slipped my mind, all right?! No need to 
jump down my throat.  
 
Elizabeth: Every weekend it’s the same thing! You 
invite over a bunch of clowns who have nothing 
better to do with their lives but get drunk and leave 
the apartment in a shambles! 
 
Nadia: Hey, don’t diss my friends! At least they’re 
fun, unlike your friends from that lame little poetry 
club. 
 
Elizabeth: You know what? I’ve had it. I don’t think I 
can live with you a second longer. 
 
Nadia: You took the words right out of my mouth. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
It slipped my mind = I 
forgot it 
 
jump down my throat 
= react angrily; make 
angry comments 
 
clowns = (informal) 
incompetent, 
ridiculous people 
 
in a shambles = in a 
complete mess 
 
diss = (slang) 
disrespect; say bad 
things about, insult 
 
lame = (slang) stupid, 
pathetic 
 
You took the words 
right out of my mouth 
= I was about to say 
the exact same thing 
Vocabulary 


 
 
Vocabulary Quiz 
Complete each sentence with a word from the box. Three words are not used.

lame 
serves you right 
snoring 
blow a fuse 
hung over 
pooped 
sleep in

clown 
in a shambles 
reeks of 
slip my mind 
trashed 
 
 
1. After holding a three-hour long birthday party with twenty kindergarteners, 
my wife and I were both ______________________. 
2. The movie was supposed to be scary, but it was actually kind of 
______________________. 
3. I can't believe Michael got promoted to director! That ______________________ has 
no clue how to manage people. 
4. You really should wash out your gym bag once in a while. It 
______________________ old sweat. 
5. My 7 AM class was canceled, so I got to ______________________. 
6. One of my coworkers always ______________________ my office without knocking 
whenever she needs something urgently. 
7. I set up reminders on my phone to pay the bills, so that it doesn't 
______________________. 
8. The whole group of tourists was arrested after they ______________________ the 
hotel room and refused to pay for it. 
9. You cheated on your girlfriend, and now you're complaining that she's giving 
you the silent treatment? It ______________________. 
10. After our train was inexplicably delayed for the third time, my friend looked 
like he was about to ______________________. 
11. I went to the party, but I only had one beer. I didn't want to overdo it and be 
______________________ for my exam in the morning. 
12. My mom can't sleep in the same room as my dad because his 
______________________ keeps her awake. 
 


 
 
Speaking Task 
Living and sharing your space with another person can be challenging! Describe 
your experience living with someone (could be a romantic partner, roommate, 
siblings, other students, etc.) – did you get along well? Did you have “house rules”? 
Were there ever any disagreements or incidents like the one in this lesson? 
 
Record your answer at www.speakpipe.com/espressoenglish or send the MP3 to 
homework@espressoenglish.net for feedback.

Lesson 45: Cooking 
 
Listen to this conversation between Mandy and her father, Nikko, who is cooking. Mark 
the statements below “True” or “False.” 
 
 
Listening Comprehension 
 
True or false according to the dialogue? 
 
1. Nikko got the burrito recipe from a cookbook 
2. He used up all the eggs to make the burritos 
3. Nikko threw away the bacon 
4. Mandy doesn't want to eat beans for breakfast 
5. Tofu is a good source of protein 
6. Mandy refuses to try Nikko's burritos 
7. Nikko has seen health benefits from his new diet 
8. Mandy's mother was a vegan 
9. Nikko is also doing exercise 
10. Mandy thinks her dad has feelings for Sharon 
11. Mandy's mother has died 
12. Mandy disapproves of Nikko and Sharon’s relationship 
 
 


 
 
Conversation Text 
 
Mandy: Morning, Dad! Mmm, something 
smells good! 
 
Nikko: I’m making vegan breakfast burritos – 
all organic. My friend Sharon taught me how to 
make them last week. She’s a real pro in the 
kitchen. 
 
Mandy: Ah, that’s great! But Dad, what 
happened to all the eggs in the fridge? I 
could’ve sworn we had at least four left. 
 
Nikko: I threw them away. Too much 
cholesterol.  
 
Mandy: Oh. So much for the omelet I wanted to 
make. Hey – the bacon’s gone, too! 
 
Nikko: Sorry, hon. I might’ve gotten a little 
overzealous when purging our food supplies. 
Health takes precedence, though. You really 
should try to go vegan sometime. It’ll help 
unclog your arteries. And Sharon says you can 
get all the protein you need from beans. 
 
Mandy: Maybe. I really don’t think I can 
stomach beans for breakfast, though. 
 
Nikko: If you knew how many rat hairs are 
allowed into each pound of processed meat, 
you’d be saying “good riddance” to the bacon. 
 
burritos = a type of Mexican 
food made of a flour tortilla 
wrapped around a filling 
 
pro = professional; very 
skilled 
 
I could’ve sworn = I was 
quite certain 
 
hon = short for “honey,” a 
term of affection 
 
overzealous = excessively 
enthusiastic 
 
purging = clearing an area of 
things that are unwanted 
 
takes precedence = is more 
important 
 
unclog = remove blockages 
 
stomach = tolerate, accept 
 
good riddance = it’s a good 
thing that’s gone 
 
Vocabulary 


 
 
Mandy: Well, ignorance is bliss. I guess I’ll try 
your burritos. But… what are those slimy white 
chunks? 
 
Nikko: It’s tofu. Another great source of 
protein, by the way! I know it doesn’t look very 
appetizing, but don’t let that put you off. The 
tofu absorbs the flavors of all the other 
ingredients. 
 
Mandy: I’ll take your word for it. I’m going to 
go check my e-mail – let me know when 
breakfast is ready. 
 
Nikko: Sure. Oh! That reminds me. Sharon sent 
me this website that has great recipes with all-
natural ingredients. I’ll forward it to you.  
 
Mandy: Wow, what’s gotten into you, Dad? 
You seem pretty gung-ho about this vegan 
thing. 
 
Nikko: I’m feeling better than I have in years! 
More energy, no more ulcers. You might want 
to give it a try. 
 
Mandy: I don’t know. A vegan diet just seems 
so bland. Plus, we were raised on all that 
delicious Greek food Mom used to cook – full of 
meat and cheese. 
 
Nikko: Hey, it wasn’t a cakewalk for me either. 
You only have twenty years of bad habits to 
break away from. I’ve had forty-eight. But 
Sharon helped me understand that eating right 
ignorance is bliss = I’m 
happier not knowing 
 
slimy = disgusting, wet, 
slippery 
 
appetizing = describes food 
that is attractive and makes 
you want to eat it 
 
put you off = repel you, 
make you have a bad 
impression 
 
absorbs = takes in 
 
I’ll take your word for it = 
I’ll assume what you’re 
saying is true 
 
what’s gotten into you? = 
you’re acting much 
differently than normal 
 
gung-ho = enthusiastic 
 
ulcers = painful irritated 
holes in the lining of the 
stomach 
 
bland = boring, without 
interesting tastes 
 
a cakewalk = something 
easily accomplished 
 
Vocabulary 


 
 
can add years to your life. Along with regular 
exercise, of course. We’re doing a yoga class 
together. 
 
Mandy: Dad… I’m beginning to think this health 
kick has more to do with Sharon than anything 
else. 
 
Nikko: What do you mean? 
 
Mandy: Back when you and Mom were still 
together, you were always gushing about her 
cooking. You used to say that was what made 
you fall for her. 
 
Nikko: Yeah, I guess I did, didn’t I? 
 
Mandy: And when you talk about Sharon, you 
get that same gleam in your eye.  
 
Nikko: Well, she is a very inspiring woman. 
 
Mandy: How about inviting her over for dinner 
tomorrow night? I’d love to meet her.

obsessive interest 
 
gushing about = saying 
extremely positive and 
affectionate things about

her

your eyes “light up” with 
excitement or love
